# International contacts

***In a previous conversation I asked if there were any international bodies that might be interested in a multilingual coding system like Allspeak. You came up with***
_UNESCO_
_ITU_
_UNDP_
_UN Global Pulse_
***Can you find suitable contact information so that I can plan to make approaches?***

Good research haul. Here's a structured contact guide for all four:

---

## Allspeak — UN/IGO Outreach Contacts

### 1. UNESCO — Division for Digital Inclusion & Policies
**Why:** UNESCO just launched its *Global Roadmap on Multilingualism in the Digital Era* and is actively looking for industry partners on language technology. The Roadmap was developed with input from over 100 organisations across 53 countries, and explicitly calls on industry to "design inclusive Language Technologies." [UNESCO](https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/unesco-launches-global-roadmap-multilingualism-digital-era)

**Key contact:**
- **Guilherme Canela de Souza Godoi** — Director, Division for Digital Inclusion and Policies
- Email: **g.godoi@unesco.org** · Phone: +33 1 45 68 10 58 [UNESCO](https://www.unesco.org/en/communication-information/whos-who)
- Also relevant: **Xianhong Hu** (Programme Specialist, multilingualism) — x.hu@unesco.org

**Approach:** Position Allspeak as a concrete implementation of the Roadmap's "Research, Development and Industry" priority area — a tool that lets developers in any language community write code in their native tongue.

---

### 2. ITU — AI for Good (Innovation Factory)
**Why:** The AI for Good Innovation Factory is the leading UN-based startup pitching and acceleration platform, offering global pitching opportunities, funding connections, expert mentorship, and media exposure. [AI for Good](https://aiforgood.itu.int/about-us/innovation-factory/)

**Key entry points:**
- **Innovation Factory** (pitch your startup) �� [aiforgood.itu.int/about-us/innovation-factory](https://aiforgood.itu.int/about-us/innovation-factory/)
- **Submit a use case** → [aiforgood.itu.int/innovate-for-impact/submit-new-ai-use-cases](https://aiforgood.itu.int/innovate-for-impact/submit-new-ai-use-cases/)
- **General engagement/partnership** → [aiforgood.itu.int/engage](https://aiforgood.itu.int/engage/)

**Upcoming event:** The AI for Good Global Summit 2026 runs 7–10 July at Palexpo, Geneva, back-to-back with the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance. [AI for Good](https://aiforgood.itu.int/inside-the-ai-for-good-global-summit-2026-where-innovation-meets-action/) This is your best near-term target — the Innovation Factory Grand Finale is there, with a $20,000 top prize.

**Approach:** Frame Allspeak as a digital inclusion tool that lowers barriers to coding for non-English-speaking communities, fitting squarely within ITU's "leave no one behind" connectivity agenda.

---

### 3. UN Global Pulse
**Why:** UN Global Pulse is a vibrant network for collaborative innovation, connecting experts from inside and outside of the UN family, and explicitly invites people to explore how to become a partner. [Unglobalpulse](https://www.unglobalpulse.org/)

**Key entry points:**
- **Partner enquiry** → [unglobalpulse.org](https://www.unglobalpulse.org/) (use the "become a partner" route on the site)
- They have hubs in Geneva, Kampala, Jakarta and Helsinki — Helsinki is particularly active on private-sector partnerships

**Approach:** UN Global Pulse is more of a research/data-science lab than a funding body, so the pitch here should be around Allspeak as a *tool for their work* — e.g. enabling local language communities to build their own data tools or monitoring dashboards without needing English-language coding skills.

---

### 4. UNDP — Digital, AI and Innovation Hub
**Why:** UNDP has specifically cited "AI for Local Languages" as a priority area, and operates Accelerator Labs in 91 locations supporting 115 countries. [United Nations](https://www.un.org/digital-emerging-technologies/sites/www.un.org.techenvoy/files/GDC-submission_UNDP.pdf)

**Key entry points:**
- **Digital hub** → [undp.org/digital](https://www.undp.org/digital)
- **Accelerator Labs Network** (most actionable) — each country lab can pilot and scale solutions independently. Find the lab nearest to a target language community at [acceleratorlabs.undp.org](https://acceleratorlabs.undp.org)

**Approach:** The Accelerator Labs model is specifically designed to test and scale tools in local contexts. Proposing a pilot of Allspeak in a specific country — perhaps one where you've already built a language variant, like Italian or Bulgarian — is a much more concrete ask than a general partnership enquiry.

| Priority | Body | Action |
|----------|------|--------|

| **Next** | UNDP Accelerator Labs | Identify a specific country lab and propose a language pilot |
| **Later** | UN Global Pulse | Reach out once you have a published case study to reference |

Would you like help drafting any of these initial outreach emails?

>***Yes I would. For context, Allspeak is currently in English and Italian. French and German are under construction and I would wait for that to complete before making any approaches.***

Good plan — having four languages including two major European ones will make the case much stronger. Let me draft all four. I'll do them one at a time.

There are your four drafts. A few notes on each:

**UNESCO** — I gave you two variants. The first is tighter and more confident; the second is warmer and explicitly takes funding off the table, which can help get a first response from someone senior who might otherwise pass it down. I'd lean toward the second for a cold approach to a director-level contact.

**ITU AI for Good** — This one is less about relationship-building and more about finding the right door, since ITU uses structured submission forms. The email asks them to direct you to the correct process rather than assuming, which is the honest position and avoids wasted effort.

**UNDP** — The Italian pilot angle is deliberate. Generic approaches to UNDP tend to disappear; offering a concrete, geographically plausible pilot gives them something to grab onto. You might want to revisit this once French is ready, since the Francophone Accelerator Labs in West Africa are particularly active.

**UN Global Pulse** — This is the most speculative of the four, so I've written it with explicit humility about fit, and asked them to redirect you if needed. That's actually a useful tactic — a "who should I talk to?" email to the wrong person often gets a warmer response than a pitch to the right person who isn't expecting you.

One general point: all four emails avoid any mention of funding or grant requests, which is right for initial contact. You want to be received as a potential partner and contributor, not as an applicant.

**UNESCO — Option 1 (Direct & concise)**
Subject: Allspeak — a multilingual programming language aligned with UNESCO's Digital Roadmap

Dear Mr Canela,

I am writing to introduce Allspeak, an open-source programming language system that allows developers to write code in their native human language. Where conventional programming languages require English syntax, Allspeak presents the same underlying logic in whichever language the developer chooses. We currently support English and Italian, with French and German at an advanced stage of development.

I was struck by UNESCO's Global Roadmap on Multilingualism in the Digital Era, and in particular its call for industry to 'design inclusive Language Technologies' and to 'lower barriers for communities with limited data or resources.' Allspeak addresses exactly this gap at the level of programming itself — not just content or interfaces, but the act of building software.

The architecture makes it straightforward to add further languages, and I believe the project has potential as both a practical tool and a framework for community-led language technology development, particularly in support of the International Decade of Indigenous Languages.

I would welcome the opportunity to share a short demonstration and explore whether there is any alignment with UNESCO's current programme of work.

Yours sincerely,
Graham

**UNESCO — Option 2 (More context, softer ask)**
Subject: Introducing Allspeak — programming in any human language

Dear Mr Canela,

I hope this message finds you well. I am an independent software developer based in the UK, and the creator of Allspeak — an open-source system that allows people to write computer programs in their own language, rather than in English.

The concept is straightforward: Allspeak separates the logic of programming from the language in which that logic is expressed. We currently support English and Italian, with French and German nearing completion. Adding further languages — including those with non-Latin scripts — is a designed-in capability, not an afterthought.

I have been following UNESCO's work on multilingualism in the digital era with great interest, and the recently published Global Roadmap resonates strongly with the motivation behind Allspeak. The digital divide is not only about connectivity or content — it extends to who is able to create software at all. At present, that group is heavily skewed toward those who can work comfortably in English.

I am not approaching with a funding request at this stage, but simply to ask whether Allspeak might be of interest to UNESCO as a case study, a pilot project partner, or a tool to share with language communities working toward digital participation.

I would be glad to arrange a short online demonstration at your convenience.

With kind regards,
Graham

**ITU AI for Good**
Subject: Allspeak — multilingual programming language for the AI for Good Innovation Factory

To the AI for Good team,

I am writing to introduce Allspeak and to enquire about participation in the AI for Good Innovation Factory.

Allspeak is an open-source programming language system that allows developers to write code in their native human language. It currently supports English and Italian, with French and German nearing completion. The architecture is designed to accommodate any language, including those with non-Latin scripts.

The problem Allspeak addresses is structural: almost every mainstream programming language requires the developer to work in English. This is a significant and largely invisible barrier for the billions of people who are competent, motivated potential developers but not English-literate. Allspeak removes that barrier by separating the logic of programming from the language in which it is expressed.

I believe this aligns directly with ITU's digital inclusion priorities and with the Innovation Factory's focus on open, scalable solutions that address global challenges. Allspeak is open-source, lightweight, and designed to be extended by communities themselves — meaning a language community can take ownership of their own variant.

I would welcome guidance on the most appropriate route to submit — whether through the Innovation Factory, the Innovate for Impact use case process, or another channel — and am happy to provide a demonstration or supporting materials.

Yours faithfully,
Graham
